info.name: Marketplace API — v1.0 (Frozen)
info.description:
Multi-Tenant SaaS Marketplace Platform backend — API contract frozen at v1.0.0 as of the Phase 5 hardening pass (covers Phases 0-4: Foundation, Product Marketplace Core, Platform & Marketplace, Service Marketplace, Unification/Reporting/Comms). See docs/API_CHANGELOG.md for what changed getting here and the freeze policy going forward. Run folders top-to-bottom on a fresh DB (after `php artisan migrate` + the RBAC seeder) and every request should work as-is — each request that creates a resource saves its id into a collection variable that later requests reuse.

Super Admin endpoints (RBAC, Super Admin, Marketplace queue, Subscriptions plan management folders) need a Super Admin user, which has no self-service registration endpoint by design (Phase 0 seeds the `super-admin` role/permissions but not a user). Create one via tinker, then paste the resulting token into `admin_token`:

```
php artisan tinker --execute="
\$admin = App\\Models\\User::create(['tenant_id'=>null,'name'=>'Root Admin','email'=>'root@platform.test','password'=>Hash::make('password123')]);
\$admin->assignRole(App\\Modules\\RBAC\\Models\\Role::withoutGlobalScopes()->where('name','super-admin')->first());
"
```
Then use the "Login (Super Admin)" request in the RBAC folder.

Phase 2 additions: Super Admin (merchants, dashboard), Marketplace (publish/approve), Subscriptions (plans, subscribe, plan-limit enforcement), Payments expansion (Stripe/PayPal/Nagad/Rocket/Bank Transfer), Shipping (rate calc, shipments, delivery webhook), Promotions (coupons, flash sales, bundle/BOGO rules). Scheduled jobs (dashboard refresh, subscription billing, flash sale activation) only run via `php artisan schedule:work` or manually via tinker — they won't fire just from hitting the API.

item.name: Social Login (Google/Facebook) — open in browser, not Postman

request.description: POST /auth/social/{provider} redirects to the OAuth provider, and GET /auth/social/{provider}/callback is hit by that provider's redirect - both are browser-driven Socialite flows, not request/response calls Postman can complete on their own. Listed here for API-surface completeness only; test by visiting the URL in a browser with a real Google/Facebook OAuth app configured.

item.name: Cleanup (run after Products - these rows are used as FKs above)

request.description: No coupon_code by default - Promotions > Coupons runs later in the collection, so a coupon wouldn't exist yet at this point in a full top-to-bottom run. To test a coupon discount, run Create Coupon first, then add "coupon_code": "{{coupon_code}}" to this body. Bundle/BOGO promotion rules and any active flash sale pricing apply automatically, no field needed for those.

Guarded state machine: pending→confirmed→processing→shipped→delivered→(returned|refunded|exchanged), or cancelled from pending/confirmed/processing. If checkout hasn't been paid yet (status still pending), use 'confirmed' first — see the Payments folder to auto-confirm via COD instead.

Moved after Checkout deliberately - removing the cart item before Checkout would leave the cart empty and Checkout would 422 with 'Cannot checkout an empty cart.'. By this point checkout has already consumed the cart, so this demonstrates removing an item from a new, now-empty cart instead (still a valid call, just an empty result).

item.name: Initiate Payment (Bank Transfer — stays pending until confirmed)

request.description: Response includes bank_details for the customer to wire funds to. No webhook exists for this gateway - use 'Confirm Bank Transfer Payment' below (staff action, after checking the bank statement) to mark it completed and confirm the order.

item.name: Confirm Bank Transfer Payment (manual, staff action)

request.description: Only works for gateway: bank_transfer payments still in 'pending' status. Marks the payment completed and confirms the order, mirroring what a webhook would do for other gateways.

item.name: Webhook (sslcommerz) — NOT directly callable from here

request.description: This will 422 as-is: the gateway signs webhook bodies with an HMAC-SHA256 signature (X-Signature header) computed against config('services.sslcommerz.store_password'), which Postman can't compute inline. To exercise this path, use the automated test in tests/Feature/PaymentWebhookIdempotencyTest.php, which builds a correctly-signed request. The same applies to bkash, stripe, paypal, nagad, and rocket webhooks - each signs against its own config secret.
Requires a Super Admin user to already exist — see the collection-level description for the tinker command to create one.
Served from cache (Cache key: admin.dashboard); computes synchronously on first call if the hourly RefreshDashboardStatsJob hasn't run yet.
Sets marketplace_status to 'pending' - awaits Super Admin review below before published_to_marketplace becomes true.

Replaces any existing active subscription. If the new plan's limits (e.g. products) are lower than current usage, further creation of that resource is blocked immediately - see plan.limit middleware on POST /products.

Deletes a throwaway plan created by this request's own pre-request script, not {{plan_id}} - that one is actively referenced by the Subscribe call earlier in this folder, and deleting a plan with a live subscription 500s on a foreign key violation rather than a clean 4xx (a real API gap worth knowing about, not a Postman issue).

exec: // {{plan_id}} is actively subscribed to by this point (Subscribe
// ran earlier in this folder) - deleting it would 500 on a FK
// violation from the subscriptions table. Create a disposable,
// never-subscribed plan just for this demo instead.
body: { mode: 'raw', raw: JSON.stringify({ name: 'Disposable', slug: 'disposable-' + Date.now(), price: 1 }) }

request.description: provider can be pathao, steadfast, redx, or sundarban - each has a different base rate/eta.

item.name: Webhook (pathao) — NOT directly callable from here

request.description: Same signed-webhook limitation as Payments - couriers sign callbacks with an HMAC-SHA256 signature (X-Signature) against each provider's own config secret, which Postman can't compute inline. When a webhook reports 'delivered', the order auto-transitions shipped -> delivered.
type is 'percentage' or 'fixed'. Referenced by {{coupon_code}} in the Orders > Checkout request.

starts_at is 'now' via Postman's {{$isoTimestamp}}; ends_at is set by this request's pre-request script to +1 hour, since the API requires ends_at to be strictly after starts_at and both resolving to the same instant (as two separate {{$isoTimestamp}} calls would) fails validation. New sales start in 'scheduled' status; the ActivateFlashSalesJob (every 5 min) flips it to 'active' once starts_at has passed, which is when CartService starts applying the discount.

buy_product_id and get_product_id are usually different products - set to the same one here only as a placeholder since the collection only tracks one {{product_id}}. Applied automatically at checkout, no coupon code needed.
config.product_ids needs at least 2 distinct product ids in a real bundle - placeholders repeated here for the same reason as the BOGO example above.

Needs a real file attached to the 'certificate' form field - only possible from the Postman GUI (Body > form-data > select a file), not from a scripted run. 422s with no file attached, same as KYC Document upload and Upload Product Image.

request.description: The booking status machine only allows sequential transitions (assigned -> on_the_way -> started -> completed), so reaching 'completed' takes 3 calls in a row - this one, then the two that follow it in this folder.

Moved to the end of this folder deliberately: reject transitions the booking to 'cancelled', a terminal state - if this ran between Accept and Assign (its natural chronological spot) it would break every later request in this folder (and Reviews) that depends on this same {{booking_id}} reaching 'completed'. Run standalone against a fresh booking to see it succeed; here it will correctly 422 since the demo booking is already 'completed' by this point.
